text:
kevin: quick heads-up — ran the short-context suite (conversational summarization + one-shot Q/A) on the new orca13b-lite int4 build. numbers look promising on cost but marginal on quality.

maria: can you drop the raw numbers?

kevin: sure — baseline (fp16 reference): latency 85ms p50, cost ~ $120 / 1M tokens. int4 build: latency 62ms p50, cost ~ $42 / 1M tokens.

ajay: nice delta on cost. what about quality metrics?

kevin: summarized: ROUGE-L down 1.8 points on the conv-sum slice, exact-match in the one-shot Q/A down 2.3%. subjective acceptability (human blind) showed failure cases ~2.7% higher.

maria: ok small but non-trivial. any particular slices where regressions concentrate?

kevin: yes — multi-turn contexts with user edits and heavy numeric reasoning. short prompts (<200 tokens) mostly fine. long-with-edit cases hit the worst drop.

olivia: from GTN/product POV — users on freemium care about latency and price. enterprise will want no regressions on longform. what are we recommending for routing?

kevin: proposal: hybrid routing + safety fallback. default -> int4. If any of these signals fire, route to int8/int16 or fallback model: 1) tokens > 300 and contains numeric tokens (regex) 2) high-entropy prompt (model-estimated perplexity > threshold) 3) user is in enterprise cohort or has opted-in for high-fidelity.

ajay: can we implement that cheaply? need a cheap classifier or heuristic at the edge. ops-bot: what do we need infra-wise?

ops-bot: rollout checklist: 
- flagged route logic as config in routing service (canary first)
- add metric: "quant_fallback_rate" per route
- add alert if fallback_rate > 10% for > 10m
- shadow traffic to int8 for 5% of requests for 24h

maria: also recommend a small eval set (50 cases) for the long-edit slice to monitor drift per deploy. we should track ROUGE-L, EM and human acceptability % weekly.

kevin: agreed. created a quick scorecard mock: 
```
slice: short-context conv-sum | FP16: RL 42.1 | INT4: RL 41.0 | delta -1.1 | cost ratio 0.35
slice: long-edit numeric  | FP16: RL 39.4 | INT4: RL 37.6 | delta -1.8 | cost ratio 0.35
human_accept: FP16 96.2% | INT4 93.5% | delta -2.7pts
unit_cost_per_1M_tokens: FP16 $120 | INT4 $42
```

kevin: recommendation options (short): 
- conservative: default to int8 for all customer traffic (retain quality, cost ~ $75 / 1M)
- hybrid (favored): default int4 + heuristics for int8/fp16 fallback (expected avg cost ~ $48 / 1M, expected quality loss <1% weighted)
- aggressive: default int4, fallback only on explicit failures (lowest cost ~ $42 / 1M but riskier)

olivia: for GTN messaging, hybrid is easiest to sell: "fast & affordable by default, high-fidelity rails when needed". enterprise SKUs can opt for conservative.

ajay: ops note — implement canary for routing and shadow int8 as ops-bot said. also log per-request quality signals (likelihood ratio, kvcache hits).

maria: one more ask for ML: run an int6 quant (or per-channel quant) quick pass — maybe we can hit latency close to int4 but with smaller reg. can we budget compute?

kevin: yes I can schedule a 48h sweep (int6 + perchannel int4 hybrid) and push results to the scorecard. FYI will need 4 x A100-80h for the sweep.

olivia: re: GTN — olivia -> @kevin can you draft a one-paragraph biz-friendly summary for the public playbook? include cost savings + fallback guarantee.

kevin: will do. rough draft: "New orca13b-lite int4 reduces inference unit cost by ~65% for short-context use cases while preserving user-perceived quality via an automated high-fidelity fallback that ensures long-context and numerically-sensitive prompts are handled by higher-precision variants."

ajay: perfect. ops-bot: set a reminder to check fallback_rate and user complaints 72h after canary starts.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled.

maria: thanks — next steps: (1) implement routing heuristics + canary (2) run int6 sweep (3) prepare scorecard + 50-case long-edit eval (4) draft GTN blurb. I'll own (3).

kevin: 👍 starting tasks now. will post the sweep stub/results in #eng-ml when done.

olivia: thanks team — leaning hybrid for initial rollout. will sync with growth on messaging later. :thumbsup:
